cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use black lettering on these moving labels. Pale blue may look pleasant, but it won't be legible from the van.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't packed any of the boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why we can still label them properly. 'Kitchen' at the top, in capitals. Leave room for a contents list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van is outside. They want to start loading.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then face every label toward the door. All the same way, please. I'll check the spelling while you turn them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 contrast, A3 label hierarchy and A5 orientation/spelling corrections turn professional moving preparation into avoidance of actual packing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 empty boxes are reframed as labeling access; B4 van loading request is reframed as orientation work.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 press the real task and arrival deadline, while A keeps B engaged in smaller work.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes the arrival of B4 loaders produce a further layer of label quality control instead of packed boxes.

specificity.evidence: A1 moving labels, B2 no packing and B4 waiting van establish the whole conflict.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 concrete turning and spelling tasks let the audience see the irony without a self-explaining empty-box punchline.
